title: Billing: support new marketplace SKU plan codes + add-on entitlements (metering + invoice descriptions)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Support new marketplace SKU taxonomy in Redwood internal billing so that (a) marketplace purchases reliably translate into the correct internal plan + entitlements, (b) usage is metered against the correct meters for that plan, and (c) invoice line item descriptions are procurement-friendly and consistent across AWS/GCP + Redwood Console.

Context
We are refreshing AWS + GCP marketplace listings with new SKUs aligned to Hosted API, Dedicated, Private, plus add-ons (e.g., compliance/retention/premium SLA where applicable). Entitlement ingestion/mapping is handled in ENG-4401 (control plane mapping layer) and webhook validation/audit logging in ENG-4402. This ticket is scoped to internal billing + metering + invoice description surfaces.

In-scope
- Add new internal plan codes that correspond to marketplace SKUs (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
- Add add-on entitlements as first-class billable flags (where applicable) and ensure they map to invoice descriptions.
- Ensure meters used for usage-based charging are correct by plan (Hosted token meters, embedding meters, etc.).
- Ensure invoice line descriptions match the marketplace SKU naming conventions (per PRD/packaging doc), including add-ons.
- Guardrails: prevent mixing incompatible plans (e.g., marketplace Hosted plan + direct-contract Private license) without explicit override.

Out-of-scope
- Re-platforming billing engine.
- New pricing model changes beyond what is required to support the marketplace SKUs.

Primary stakeholders
- Billing Eng: Cole Summers (assignee)
- Metering: Nadia Rahman (reviewer)
- PM (packaging): Nikhil Sharma, Lauren Bishop, Vivek Kulkarni
- Finance: Laura Bennett / Rishi Malhotra (invoice/revrec review)
- Partnerships: (for marketplace nomenclature parity)

Proposed internal representation (draft; final names must match PM-873 / ADR)
Base plans (examples)
- plan.marketplace.hosted.v2
- plan.marketplace.dedicated.v2
- plan.marketplace.private.v2

Add-on entitlements (examples)
- addon.marketplace.compliance_pack (drives compliance attachment access + retention statements in contract packet; non-functional enforcement handled elsewhere)
- addon.marketplace.audit_log_retention_365d (controls retention tier in Console + backend enforcement)
- addon.marketplace.premium_sla (controls SLA support tier + support routing)

Note: Dedicated and Private may have marketplace packaging that is not purely usage-based; invoice description still needs to be correct even if charges are marketplace-side. We still need internal representation for entitlement and support gating.

Functional requirements
1) Plan code support
- Billing service recognizes new plan codes from entitlement mapping layer.
- Plan codes are versioned ("v2") to avoid collision with existing marketplace buyers on legacy SKUs.
- Backward compatibility: legacy marketplace plan codes remain valid until migration window ends.

2) Meter selection and attribution
- Hosted marketplace plans map to the same underlying meters as direct Hosted plans (token in/out, embeddings units), unless PM/Finance explicitly define a marketplace-specific meter.
- Dedicated marketplace plans must not start usage-based token metering by default unless required for internal cost attribution (needs explicit confirmation).
- Private marketplace plans: no token metering for billing; allow metering for cost attribution only if it does not leak into invoice.

3) Invoice description formatting
- For any internally-generated invoice artifacts (and for Console billing views), display friendly names:
  - “Redwood Inference — Hosted API (Marketplace)”
  - “Redwood Inference — Dedicated Capacity (Marketplace)”
  - “Redwood Inference — Private Deployment License (Marketplace)”
  - Add-ons appear as separate line items when present:
    - “Compliance Pack (Marketplace Add-on)”
    - “Audit Log Retention — 365 days (Marketplace Add-on)”
    - “Premium SLA (Marketplace Add-on)”
- Avoid security/compliance claims in line items beyond the approved naming (PMM/Security language).

4) Transitions / upgrades / downgrades
- Respect PM-876 policy for upgrades/downgrades:
  - Changing base plan via marketplace should create a new entitlement event and transition the internal plan with proration behavior defined by Finance.
  - Add-ons should be attachable/detachable independent of base plan where marketplace supports it.
- Ensure internal plan transition logic does not accidentally cancel service when marketplace entitlement events are delayed/replayed (idempotent updates).

5) Validation / error handling
- If entitlement mapping layer passes an unknown plan code, surface a hard error to provisioning pipeline with a clear message ("Unknown marketplace plan code: …") and include remediation steps.
- If add-on entitlement arrives without a compatible base plan, allow storing it but do not activate until base plan present; emit alert.

Acceptance criteria
- New plan codes are deployed to production with feature flag control and are recognized by billing service.
- Meter selection tests cover Hosted marketplace plan mapping for:
  - chat/generate token meters
  - embeddings meter
  - rerank meter (if applicable in catalog)
- Invoice description strings are reviewed by Finance and PMM and match the SKU naming guidelines.
- Integration test fixture exists (ENG-4410) demonstrating:
  - base plan only
  - base + 1 add-on
  - base + multiple add-ons
  - replayed entitlement events do not duplicate plan transitions or invoice items
- Runbook note added for Support (link to CS guide) indicating what to check when a buyer reports invoice description mismatch.

Risks / open questions
- Marketplace fees/credit representation: confirm we do not attempt to represent marketplace credits/discounts in Redwood invoice UI beyond "Marketplace billed" indicator.
- Dedicated/Private pricing: confirm whether internal billing should create $0 invoices for marketplace buyers (likely no) vs just showing entitlement state.
- Add-on bundling differences between AWS and GCP: ensure our internal model supports platform-specific availability without creating plan code sprawl.

Implementation notes (engineering)
- Add plan codes and add-on flags to billing-plan registry.
- Update mapping table from plan -> allowed meters (Hosted only).
- Update invoice rendering layer to use the new display strings, including a "(Marketplace)" suffix.
- Add a guard that marketplace plans cannot be combined with direct-contract enterprise license unless org has override flag (to be set by Finance/RevOps).

Links
- PRD: cloud marketplace listing refresh (Confluence)
- Packaging catalog v2 (Confluence)
- ADR: marketplace SKU naming + entitlement IDs (Confluence)
- ENG-4401: entitlement mapping layer
- ENG-4402: webhook validation + audit logs
- PM-876: upgrade/downgrade policy

Definition of Done
- Code merged + deployed behind flag.
- Finance approved invoice descriptions.
- Integration tests passing in CI.
- Launch readiness checklist item "Billing/SKU support" checked by Release Eng (Connor O’Brien).
comments: 2025-01-17 (Cole Summers): Initial pass at plan registry updates. Blocked pending final plan code strings from PM-873; I added placeholders with v2 suffix so we don’t collide with legacy marketplace plans.

2025-01-23 (Nadia Rahman): Metering note — Hosted marketplace should use the same meters as Hosted direct to keep cost attribution consistent. For Dedicated/Private, strongly prefer cost-attribution-only metrics that are NOT surfaced in invoices or customer billing exports.

2025-01-28 (Laura Bennett): Invoice naming: keep it procurement friendly and avoid implying certifications. “Compliance Pack” is fine; do not include “SOC 2” or “ISO” in invoice line items. Also add “(Marketplace)” suffix so AP teams can reconcile.

2025-02-03 (Cole Summers): Implemented invoice display string layer for marketplace plans/add-ons. Next: enforce compatibility rules and add unknown-plan hard error path. Will sync with Ethan Park on error propagation from entitlement mapping.

2025-02-10 (Talia Benson): Please ensure this is covered by ENG-4410 fixtures for AWS and GCP. Partner review flagged that GCP sometimes emits entitlement updates out-of-order; idempotency here is a must.
